name: A Brown County woods lot

place_source.title: Wikidata: Nashville, Indiana (Q1924785), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A rural woods lot south of Nashville, Indiana, at the edge of the oak-hickory forest over Brown County: white and red oak, hickory and beech overhead, a redcedar and a white pine on cleared ground, dogwood and redbud below. Wild turkeys and deer work the leaf litter and the mast, squirrels and chipmunks run the trunks, and a southern flying squirrel glides between the cavities after dark.

facts.text: Nashville, the town at the centre of Brown County, Indiana, lies at about 39.21 degrees north, 86.25 degrees west and about 181 m above sea level.

source.title: Wikidata: Nashville, Indiana (Q1924785), coordinate location (P625) and elevation above sea level (P2044)

facts.text: Nashville has a humid subtropical climate (Köppen Cfa), characterised by hot, humid summers and generally mild to cool winters.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Nashville, Indiana", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Nashville, Indiana", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Brown County State Park lies in the centre of the southern half of Indiana, and its trees include black, sugar, red and silver maple, American beech, basswood, black cherry, black gum and red elm.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Brown County State Park", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Brown County State Park", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Mammals typically found in Brown County State Park include white-tailed deer, bobcats, opossums, eastern gray squirrels and chipmunks.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Brown County State Park", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Brown County State Park", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Most of Brown County's forests were cleared between the 1840s and the end of the nineteenth century, and the resulting poor farming practice and erosion depleted the county's soil nutrients.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Brown County State Park", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Brown County State Park", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Wild turkeys prefer hardwood and mixed conifer-hardwood forest with scattered openings such as pastures, fields, orchards and seasonal marshes, and in the northeastern United States they are most profuse in oak-hickory timber.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Wild turkey", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Wild turkey", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The southern flying squirrel is nocturnal, feeds on fruits and nuts from trees such as red and white oak, hickory and beech, and glides between them on the membrane between its fore and hind limbs.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Southern flying squirrel", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Southern flying squirrel", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
